Project: operator-visibility
Repo: ai-os — you are already inside its worktree (branch project/8ea0cc08, off main).
Project brief: ## Goal
Make the operator's agent activity genuinely legible to Konrad: a Live panel that is fast and truthful, and a chat surface that shows the operator's communication with its agents. Konrad's words this morning: hovering the sidebar still lags; he cannot tell 'whether these are sub-agents of Claude Fable 5 or actually whole Claude Code sessions'; elapsed times 'are still growing even though they are done'; and in the operator chat he wants to 'see the conversations you have with them... something similar to the bash command, where I can see that you sent them a message and that you received a message from them.'

## Context
Repos in this worktree: forge-control (Hono :7700) and forge-control-web (Next 15 + React 19, pm2 forge-control-web). Live panel: app/desktop/live/AgentActivity.tsx, ManagersSection.tsx, agentsApi.ts; feed comes from /api/agents (forge-control/src/routes/agents.ts) and /api/projects/managers. Chat thread rendering: the desktop chat surface under app/desktop/ — find how Bash tool calls are rendered as collapsible blocks and mirror that pattern. Run rows live in the `runs` table (metadata.role, metadata.project_id, parent_run_id for sub-agent runs, started_at/updated_at, status). Design tokens: app/tokens.ts — CSS variables, both themes must work, zero hardcoded colors.

## Definition of done
1. TIME TRUTH: a settled run (completed/failed/cancelled) shows a FROZEN duration (settled_at - started_at). Only live runs tick. No exceptions anywhere in the panel.
2. KIND TRUTH: every row is visibly classified: full Claude Code session runs (project workers with their role: architect/planner/builder/reviewer/scout/researcher, and operator chats) vs in-process sub-agents (parent_run_id children), with the model it ran on and, on hover, its parent/lineage. A stranger should be able to read the panel and understand the org chart of a running project.
3. HOVER PERFORMANCE: hovering rows causes no visible lag. Profile first (React DevTools profiler or equivalent measurement in the planning corpus), find the actual cause (re-render storm, expensive tooltip mount, layout thrash, over-polling), fix it, and record before/after numbers.
4. AGENT COMMS IN CHAT: in the operator chat thread, messages the operator sends to agents and results/notifications it receives back render as first-class collapsible blocks in the transcript — direction marker + agent name + one-line preview, expandable to the full payload — visually consistent with how Bash tool blocks render. The data already exists in the run's thread JSON (tool_use / tool_result entries for Agent/SendMessage and task notifications); render it, don't invent a new pipeline. If specific payloads truly are not in the thread, document exactly what is missing instead of building new plumbing.
5. npx tsc --noEmit clean in both repos; npm run build passes in forge-control-web.

## Quality bar
Reviewers must run tsc + the web build, curl the touched endpoints, and verify both themes. For the hover fix, the reviewer must see the recorded before/after measurement, not take the builder's word.

## Constraints / hard rules
- Design tokens only. pnpm repos: NODE_ENV=development pnpm add X --prod=false.
- NEVER restart or touch forge-executor. Restarting forge-control and forge-control-web is allowed.
- Do NOT touch Files components (FileExplorerPanel*, VaultFileList*, routes/files.ts) — recently shipped by another project.
- Do NOT touch forge-control/src/lib/project-tick.ts, cc-runner.ts, executor.ts or db/projects.ts — a parallel project (engine-v2-research-lane) owns engine internals this cycle. If a small runs-query change in routes/agents.ts needs a db helper, put it in routes/agents.ts's own query, not in shared engine files.
- Work ONLY inside this worktree until the deploy phase. Never edit the live checkout /opt/forge-ai-os during build phases.

## Deployment (final phase, only after reviewer PASS)
1. In /opt/forge-ai-os: merge main INTO your work branch first if main moved, re-run tsc + build in the worktree, then merge your branch to main. On any conflict: STOP, leave the branch, report exactly which files.
2. Rebuild forge-control-web, pm2 restart forge-control-web (and forge-control only if API files changed). NEVER forge-executor.
3. Verify pm2 online, :7700/api/health ok, web serves. Summarize changes + the hover before/after numbers in your final message.

### Verbatim SQL — `fetchActiveRows` (agents.ts:420–449)

```sql
SELECT id::text, title, status, worker, spent_usd::text,
       metadata,
       CASE
         WHEN metadata ? 'rollup_v1' THEN NULL::jsonb
         WHEN status IN ('running','queued','paused','stuck') THEN thread
         ELSE NULL::jsonb
       END AS thread,
       parent_run_id::text AS parent_run_id,
       started_at::text, updated_at::text, last_heartbeat_at::text
  FROM runs
 WHERE (
         status IN ('running','queued','paused','stuck')
         OR (status IN ('completed','failed','cancelled')
             AND updated_at > now() - ($1 || ' milliseconds')::interval)
       )
       ${projectFilter}
 ORDER BY
   CASE status
     WHEN 'running' THEN 0
     WHEN 'paused'  THEN 1
     WHEN 'stuck'   THEN 2
     WHEN 'queued'  THEN 3
     ELSE 4
   END,
   started_at DESC NULLS LAST,
   updated_at DESC
 LIMIT 60
```

`projectFilter` (agents.ts:417–418), only when `?project_id=` present:
```sql
AND metadata->>'project_id' = $2
AND metadata->>'role' IS DISTINCT FROM 'manager'
```
`$1 = RECENT_COMPLETION_WINDOW_MS = 24*60*60*1000` (agents.ts:145).

### Verbatim SQL — `fetchStatusRollup` (agents.ts:461–469)

```sql
SELECT
   COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'running')::text AS running,
   COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'queued')::text  AS queued,
   COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'stuck')::text   AS stuck,
   COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'paused')::text  AS paused
  FROM runs
 WHERE archived = false
```

### Verbatim SQL — `fetchHourlyTotals` (agents.ts:485–496)

```sql
SELECT
   COALESCE(SUM(spent_usd), 0)::text AS spent_usd,
   COALESCE(SUM(
     COALESCE((metadata->'usage_last_turn'->>'input_tokens')::bigint, 0)
   ), 0)::text AS input_tokens,
   COALESCE(SUM(
     COALESCE((metadata->'usage_last_turn'->>'output_tokens')::bigint, 0)
   ), 0)::text AS output_tokens
  FROM runs
 WHERE updated_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
```

### Verbatim SQL — `GET /api/agents/:id` (agents.ts:661–669)

```sql
SELECT id::text, title, status, worker, spent_usd::text,
       metadata, thread, parent_run_id::text AS parent_run_id,
       started_at::text, updated_at::text, last_heartbeat_at::text
  FROM runs
 WHERE id = $1
 LIMIT 1
```

### Settled-timestamp question — answer: **NO**

- The response contains **no** `settled_at`, `completed_at`, `ended_at`, or `finished_at`. Neither SELECT in agents.ts lists `completed_at` at all, and `AgentRun` has no such field.
- It **does** include `parent_run_id` (agents.ts:584) and `model` (agents.ts:559).
- It does **not** include `metadata.role` or `metadata.project_id` — both exist in the DB and are used by the query's WHERE clause, but neither is projected into `AgentRun`. There is no way for the client to tell an `architect` row from a `builder` row, or which project a run belongs to.
- Grep for `settled_at|ended_at|finished_at` across `forge-control/src` + `forge-control-web/app` yields only three hits, all in `run-rollup.ts` (58, 191, 228) — the per-**subagent** `ended_at`. See §5.

It is **Postgres**, not sqlite — `content_forge` DB at `127.0.0.1:5432`.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS runs (
  id                   uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  title                text NOT NULL,
  prompt               text NOT NULL,
  worker               varchar(64),
  status               varchar(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued'
                         CHECK (status IN ('queued','running','paused','stuck',
                                           'completed','failed','cancelled')),
  thread               jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  budget_usd           numeric(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  spent_usd            numeric(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  parent_run_id        uuid REFERENCES runs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  stuck_signal         varchar(64),
  metadata             jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at           timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at           timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  started_at           timestamptz,
  completed_at         timestamptz,
  last_heartbeat_at    timestamptz
);
ALTER TABLE runs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS archived boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false;
```

**Server (`agents.ts:537–538`), unconditional on status:**
```ts

const elapsed = Number.isFinite(startedMs) ? Math.max(0, nowMs - startedMs) : null;
```
`nowMs = Date.now()` (agents.ts:596). There is no `status` check and `completed_at` is never selected, so `elapsed_ms` for a run that finished 5 hours ago is `now - started_at` — a value that increases by 4000ms on every poll, forever, until the row falls out of the 24h window.

**Client (`AgentActivity.tsx:136–140`):**
```ts
const live = a.status === "running";
const started = parseTs(a.started_at);
const elapsed = live && Number.isFinite(started) ? now - started : a.elapsed_ms;
```

**What shipped** — commit `9442d75` on `project/8ea0cc08` (pushed to origin): `docs/plan/00-vision.md` through `04-phases.md`, replacing the previous project's corpus. Five planner tasks seeded at rounds 100/200/300/400/500, all tier standard.

**The plan, and the recon that grounds it** (two scouts + my own reads of the Live panel, verified against the live DB):

1. **Phase 1 — Time truth.** Root cause found: `routes/agents.ts:537` computes `elapsed_ms = now − started_at` unconditionally — a 130-second completed run currently reads "5h 05m" and grows 4s per poll. The fix is pure projection: `runs.completed_at` is already populated on every completed/failed row (`COALESCE` with `updated_at` covers 4 legacy cancelled rows), and each sub-agent's `ended_at` is already persisted in the rollup but dropped by the API. No executor change needed — critical, since engine files belong to the parallel engine-v2 lane.
2. **Phase 2 — Kind truth.** `metadata.role` and `project_id` exist in every worker row but are never projected; sub-agents even carry a human `description` that's thrown away. The API gains an explicit `agent_kind` (operator/worker/cron/unknown — unknown renders honestly, never guessed); lineage arrives via enriched native `title` attributes so it can't regress hover performance.
3. **Phase 3 — Hover perf.** The Live panel has no JS hover handlers at all; the `useState`-per-row hover lives in the chat rail (`ChatListItem`). The corpus binds a measurement protocol: a committed Playwright + Chrome-tracing sweep script, baseline traces before any fix commit, a named mechanism with trace evidence, and a numeric gate (zero >50ms hover tasks, ≥50% scripting reduction) — plus a red-team reviewer briefed to attack the fix and the measurement itself.
4. **Phase 4 — Agent comms.** Agent spawns and SendMessage exchanges are already in `runs.thread` and already flow through the generic tool-block renderer; the work is `tools.by_name` renderers cloning the Bash block's grammar with direction markers. One hard gap, verified in code and DB: **agent completion notifications never reach the thread** (`cc-runner.ts` drops them; closed event union). Per the brief's escape hatch, phase 4 documents that precisely for the engine lane instead of plumbing it.
5. **Phase 5 — Deploy**, per the brief's runbook, with the one foreseeable merge conflict (docs/plan vs main's old corpus) pre-resolved as "ours" and everything else a hard stop.

22 numbered requirements, each mapped to exactly one phase; quality gates require pasted command output, both-theme screenshots, and reproduced perf numbers before PASS. The engine takes it from here — round 100's planner is next up.
